claims.text: Greg Short asserts that moonshot goals should be revisited and replaced every 6-12 months, with each successive moonshot being larger than the prior one. The mechanism is that each completed journey builds wisdom that must be carried forward and applied to the next, bigger goal, while the prior tactics and structures are scrapped. A moonshot that stops growing signals that the revision cadence has been skipped.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies to entrepreneurial goal-setting across any stage
claims.mechanism: Completing one moonshot-scale pursuit produces accumulated wisdom (pattern recognition, hard-won context) that is the only useful input to the next pursuit; the tactics and structures that served the previous goal do not transfer and must be discarded, leaving only the distilled insight.

practices.text: Identify your current moonshot goal right now. Every 6-12 months, scrap everything you built around the prior moonshot, retain the wisdom from that journey, and apply it to the next, larger moonshot.
